# Saydraft

> Speak messy. Paste polished. Local voice dictation for Windows, with local speech recognition, cleanup, and a searchable Hub. Open source under MIT; downloaded models and dependencies retain separate licenses.

Saydraft is in active development. Source setup is available; no installer release is published yet. Native/manual Windows acceptance, owner ASR accuracy acceptance, and several roadmap features remain open. Do not describe the project as complete parity or infer accuracy from its test counts.

## Source setup

Use Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Python 3.13, Git, a microphone, and free disk space for selected models. In PowerShell:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/tanzir71/saydraft.git
cd saydraft
py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv\Scripts\python -m saydraft
```

The legacy tools/build.ps1 awaits the P8 clean-environment rewrite; it is not the supported installation path. Development checks are in CONTRIBUTING.md and .github/workflows/ci.yml.

## Models and downloads

Fresh profiles recommend Parakeet v3 int8 with a language detector (773.4 MB combined). Parakeet v2 int8 is an English option (661.3 MB). Whisper base/small/medium are alternatives. The optional All languages Whisper large-v3-turbo model (1,621.7 MB) supports multilingual recognition, including Bengali and Arabic. Both languages share the same download; there are no separate language packs.

At least one compatible speech model is required for dictation. Source installation does not bundle model weights. Speech setup requires an explicit download after size/license disclosure; AI cleanup weights are optional and rules-only dictation does not need them.

Setup shows model sizes and licenses before an explicit Download action, with progress and pause/resume. Selecting a language or model starts no transfer. Later launches reuse installed weights; language pins and automatic routing use compatible installed models. New installations use %LOCALAPPDATA%\Saydraft\models\<id>\<version>; compatible legacy models remain readable in place.

## First-run setup

The wizard has six pages: Welcome, Microphone, Set up models, Shortcut, Try it, and Style quick pick. Refresh inputs explicitly discovers devices; Test input is a ten-second level-only check without transcription or saved audio. Check this PC produces a provisional capability recommendation, not a measured tier. Use speech recommendation stages the speech model without downloading or enabling AI cleanup.

Download / Resume is explicit. Setup checks installed pinned dependencies asynchronously and displays per-file transfer/checksum progress separately from whole-package verification. Finish merges changed microphone/model/shortcut/style-tone choices into the latest preferences and refuses shortcut conflicts; Cancel preserves saved preferences. Downloaded files are separate from preference saving. Next requires a verified installed package or a successfully checked existing local Whisper model. Finish verifies the current model asynchronously before saving; cancellation, hiding or navigation revokes even queued success. Missing/changed files preserve preferences.

Shortcut setup provides a Wispr-compatible preset, manual entry, and explicit press-to-learn for up to ten seconds in the focused setup window. Learning reserves the idle worker, suppresses its chord through a temporary native hook, publishes only after observed cleanup, and cancels on focus/page/window changes. Check other app conflicts is an explicit read-only Wispr Flow advisory; other apps' custom bindings are unknown. Native physical/manual acceptance remains open.

Try it uses the selected microphone and installed ASR with the real cleanup processor, private in-memory History/delivery ports, and owned chat/email fields. Preparation opens no input; capture starts only on a shortcut or Record, with a one-minute cap. Practice has no audio-retention or persistent-History path, no foreground field is inspected, no clipboard is read, and no external insertion or Enter occurs. Before/after text and plain-text edit chips show actual changes. Cancellation, target/window changes, stale generations, settings replacement and shutdown retire owned work; unknown cleanup blocks completion and requests restart. External stop does not automatically restart practice. The user can skip recording.

For unavailable practice models, return to Set up models and explicitly install the selected package. For input failures, return to Microphone and check the staged device. After an external stop or Settings change, choose Prepare practice explicitly when idle. If retirement cannot be confirmed, cancel setup and restart as prompted. The one-minute practice limit is separate from daily dictation's twenty-minute default cap.

Style quick pick stages Casual/Formal for Messages/Email while preserving existing Very casual, intensity, other groups, and unchanged newer settings. A labeled rules preview uses the last practice transcript or an explicit example. It does not enable/download AI. Finish waits for observed practice retirement, saves changes once and opens Hub Home.

Check model performance explicitly measures the staged installed recognizer on the serial worker, with offline loading, a bundled eight-second fixture, one warm-up and three timed speech samples excluding preparation. Enabled installed cleanup supplies its existing exact 60-token samples; unavailable rates stay unmeasured. Successful source:onboarding reports append beside the selected configuration and inform Auto without changing a manual tier or enabling AI. Cancellation is checked between native operations; admission and Finish remain blocked until observed retirement. Failed/cancelled work keeps previous reports; stale/hidden or different-model UI results cannot publish. Completed reports are separate from Cancelled setup preference edits.

Readiness gates and an explicit read-only Windows microphone privacy diagnostic are implemented. The diagnostic queries the current Saydraft process without requesting access, discovering devices, opening input or saving settings; hiding/closing rejects late results. Allowed does not establish device usability, and unknown is not permission. Physical Windows checks, privacy-toggle acceptance, and fresh-profile manual timing acceptance remain open under P6.4. See https://github.com/tanzir71/saydraft/blob/main/docs/ONBOARDING.md. Do not infer owner accuracy or full product parity from fixture tests.

Existing local Whisper directories and HF cache snapshots are read in place. Unpinned files require successful offline loading/recognition and a matching in-memory file-freshness receipt; changed files or moved aliases require a fresh engine. This is separate from catalog SHA-256 verification and accuracy acceptance. Runtime HF entrypoints force cache-only access without stored credentials, including the tokenizer Python binding; explicit model transfers continue through pinned manifest URLs. No readiness check downloads, migrates, rewrites or prunes owner models.

## Optional AI cleanup

Optional AI cleanup is disabled by default. Explicit setup offers pinned Qwen3.5 0.8B or 2B Q4_K_M with a local llama.cpp CPU or Vulkan runtime. Recommendations do not enable or download cleanup. Validated output can fall back to deterministic rules. See docs/MODELS.md, docs/ASR_ROUTING.md, and docs/CLEANUP_SETUP.md for requirements, measurements, and limits.

Current cleanup evidence retains ten complete CPU/RTX forced-quality runs at source 4a1e69a. Fresh policy replays at 1486b09 both complete 556 golden and 100 adversarial cases without timeouts. RTX 2B accepts 269 golden replies; CPU 0.8B keeps rules throughout at 20.74 tok/s and earns no hybrid credit. The combined evidence check refuses qualification. The original CPU overrun and failed uncached interruption probe remain retained alongside successful controlled deadline/cached-input interruption checks. These measurements do not establish ASR accuracy, hardware tiers, release latency or a model default. See docs/CLEANUP_EVIDENCE.md.

Normal post-rules AI cleanup at intensities 1–3 checks content-word identity and order with bounded English grammar exceptions. Unknown substitutions, deletion, or reordering fall back to rules. Polished (intensity 4) allows broader rewording; an internal translation contract has separate similarity rules, but no user-facing Translate feature is implemented. Existing protected-detail checks still apply. This is conservative validation, not proof of semantic equivalence. See docs/VALIDATOR_V2.md and docs/CLEANUP_GATE.md.

## App behavior

1. Hold Ctrl+Win to record; F9 and XButton1 are configurable alternatives. Ctrl+Win+Space toggles hands-free mode; two short recording-shortcut taps also lock it. Esc cancels.
2. Local Parakeet or Whisper transcribes; rules handle fillers, repetitions, self-corrections, punctuation, and lists. Optional local AI cleanup, per-app styles, Dictionary, and Snippets refine output.
3. History stores raw and cleaned text before attempted delivery into the original target. Focus changes, protected fields, and elevated targets can prevent delivery; saved text remains reviewable in History.
4. Shift+Alt+Z pastes the last dictation. F10 captures to History without foreground insertion. Fresh profiles warn at 19 minutes and cap recordings at 20; saved custom bindings/limits remain unchanged.

One Hub contains Home statistics/recent dictations, global History search/changes/export/retry, Dictionary, Snippets, Style, Notes, and Settings. Win+Alt+S opens a floating plain-text Scratchpad with local autosave; Hub Notes supports search and reopening notes. Ctrl+Win+D opens the latest global History diff. Both actions can be rebound/disabled; queued requests are revoked on stop/restart. Saving/new/open/close/Quit wait for current edits, and revision conflicts retain unsaved text with save-as-new recovery. Notes share schema v3 history.db without adding dictation entries or Home statistics. See docs/NOTES.md. Physical Windows shortcut acceptance remains open; Command, Translate, Ask, and Notetaker remain roadmap work.

## Privacy and evidence

Dictation has no cloud fallback or telemetry. Audio retention is off by default; optional Keep forever / Keep N days policies preserve History text when eligible recordings expire. Retry requires retained audio. Python networking is restricted to loopback, requested model downloads and saved opt-in GitHub update checks (off by default). Complete native/helper-process firewall enforcement remains release work; the read-only firewall-rule check does not establish full coverage. See docs/PRIVACY.md.

The public website example is a canned simulation and requests no microphone access. Dated benchmark reports describe their recorded source/corpus, not automatic current-source or owner accuracy acceptance. Preserve historical report bytes and distinguish implementation from acceptance.

Current automated gates require 556 cleanup golden cases and 100 authored adversarial validator cases. The pre-word-guard baseline exposed a French substitution, then all ten forced-model jobs completed after that guard was fixed. The transport now enforces per-I/O deadlines without per-request watchdog threads and reduces idle-timer churn. Fresh CPU/RTX policy measurements complete, but rules-only CPU results cannot satisfy the accepted-model requirement; mandatory native-evidence CI wiring remains pending. Do not label partial runs or raw decoder rates as completed quality, hardware-tier, or release-latency acceptance. See docs/CLEANUP_EVIDENCE.md and its dated immutable reports.

The combined native soak at 2d96f62 completes 200 consecutive cycles with measured 3.50% current-process RSS growth, 200 matching History/paste events, zero memory-clipboard restoration failures, 100 genuine length-limited streams and all 100 sidecars exited after shutdown. The canonical tools/soak.py requires clean, isolated full native runs, positive RSS readings, complete cycle counts and verified teardown. It uses actual Inserter logic with memory clipboard/keyboard and does not exercise the owner's Windows input/clipboard. See docs/SOAK.md and eval/soak/results/2026-11-14-native/README.md. Physical Windows, ASR/tier/latency and model-quality acceptance remain separate.

CONTRIBUTING.md includes focused setup checks and the optional SAYDRAFT_TEST_PARAKEET_V3_MODEL fixture root for a real-recognizer smoke using tests/fixtures/hello.wav. Synthetic hooks/input and private profiles keep this separate from owner microphone, clipboard, desktop and physical shortcut acceptance. The archived docs/history/CODEX_HANDOFF_v1.md describes earlier VoiceTray milestones; its defaults and loop instructions are superseded by the current root plan and source.

tools.bench matrix implements the written 3/10/30/90-second cold/warm release-latency measurement with fresh processes, real-time public-fixture capture, the actual worker, SQLite-before-Inserter memory paste and observed native exits. Lite uses Whisper base; Standard/Pro use Parakeet/LID, with actual ASR identity checked per case. Full runs require twenty samples in every cell, pinned VAD, isolation and clean unchanged source. Completion, latency, actual model use and decoder rates remain separate gates; debug runs cannot qualify. The earlier Parakeet-as-Lite full attempt was stopped at 118 cases and remains an unqualified partial rules baseline. Full native matrix qualification remains pending. See docs/LATENCY_MATRIX.md; the historical warm 3/8/20-second probe retains its original scope.
